title: 1980 AHSME Problem 25

concepts.label: Sum of first n odd numbers

statement: In the nondecreasing sequence of odd integers \[ \begin{aligned} (a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots) ={}&(1,3,3,3,\\ &5,5,5,5,5,\ldots) \end{aligned} \] each positive odd integer \(k\) appears \(k\) times. It is a fact that there are integers \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) such that, for all positive integers \(n,\) \[ a_n=b\left\lfloor\sqrt{n+c}\right\rfloor+d, \] where \(\lfloor x\rfloor\) denotes the largest integer not exceeding \(x.\) The sum \(b+c+d\) equals

solutions.text:
The final occurrence of \(2m-1\) is in position \[ 1+3+\cdots+(2m-1)=m^2. \] Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} a_n&=2\left\lceil\sqrt n\right\rceil-1\\ &=2\left\lfloor\sqrt{n-1}\right\rfloor+1. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(b=2,\) \(c=-1,\) and \(d=1,\) so \(b+c+d=2.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: The first \(m\) positive odd integers have sum \(m^2\)
Express the least \(m\) with \(m^2\ge n\) using a floor of \(\sqrt{n-1}\)
